items.value: Administration of Justice, Land Revenue and Police were Reserved subjects (1, 3 and 4)
items.reasoning: Under the dyarchy of the Government of India Act 1919, Reserved subjects stayed with the Governor and his Executive Council and covered the coercive and revenue core of the state: law and order/police, administration of justice, land revenue, irrigation, famine relief, factories and labour. Transferred subjects went to ministers responsible to the legislature and covered the 'nation-building' departments: local self-government, education, public health, sanitation, agriculture, industries and excise. Statement 2, Local Self-Government, is therefore Transferred, which rules out A, B and D and leaves 1, 3 and 4.

items.value: Fanam was a coin
items.reasoning: The fanam (panam) was a small gold or silver coin of medieval and early-modern South India, current under the Vijayanagara rulers and later adopted by the Europeans in their South Indian mints, where it circulated as a fraction of the pagoda. It is a monetary unit, not clothing, ornament or weaponry.

items.value: Only Rash Behari Bose was actively associated with the Ghadar Party
items.reasoning: Rash Behari Bose took over the leadership of the planned February 1915 Ghadar rising in India and is the one name here genuinely tied to the Ghadar movement. Barindra Kumar Ghosh, brother of Aurobindo, belonged to the Bengal revolutionary stream, the Anushilan Samiti and the Alipore Bomb Case, while Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee was an Anushilan/HSRA man of the Kakori conspiracy. Neither of the latter two was a Ghadarite, so only statement 3 stands.

items.value: Both statements about the Cripps proposals are correct
items.reasoning: The Cripps draft declaration of 1942 provided for a constitution-making body drawn from the lower houses of the provincial legislatures together with representatives sent by the rulers of the Indian States, so statement 1 describes the composition correctly, though loosely, since the provincial members were to be elected by proportional representation rather than nominated. Statement 2 is squarely correct: a province unwilling to accept the new constitution could retain its existing constitutional position and Britain undertook to negotiate a separate agreement giving it the same status as the Indian Union, the 'local option' clause the Congress objected to. The judgement call is the word 'nominated' in statement 1; if that is read strictly the answer would fall to B.

items.value: Parishishtaparvan and Trishashtilakshana Mahapurana are the Jaina texts (2 and 4 only)
items.reasoning: Parishishtaparvan is Hemachandra's Sanskrit appendix to his Trishashtishalakapurushacharita, a Jaina work, and the Trishashtilakshana Mahapurana of Jinasena and Gunabhadra is the great Digambara Jaina purana. The other two are Buddhist: Nettipakarana is a Pali paracanonical treatise placed in the Khuddaka Nikaya, and Avadanashataka is a Sanskrit collection of a hundred Buddhist avadanas.

items.value: Only two pairs are correct, namely Dignaga as a Buddhist scholar and Nathamuni as a Vaishnava scholar
items.reasoning: Dignaga was the great Buddhist logician who founded the pramana school, and Nathamuni was the Srivaishnava acharya who recovered and organised the Alvars' Divya Prabandham, so pairs 2 and 3 hold. Aryadeva, however, was a Buddhist Madhyamika, the pupil of Nagarjuna and author of the Chatuhshataka, not a Jaina scholar, so pair 1 fails.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct: a Mongol assault under Ala-ud-din Khalji reached and besieged Delhi
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: the first Mongol appearance on India's frontier was in 1221 under Chingiz Khan pursuing Jalal-ud-din Mangbarni to the Indus, during Iltutmish's reign, long before Jalal-ud-din Khalji. Statement 2 is right: in 1299 Qutlugh Khwaja and again in 1303 Targhi advanced on Delhi, the latter blockading the city while Ala-ud-din sheltered in Siri. That combination eliminates A, C and D and forces B. Note that statement 3 is also defensible on many accounts of Tarmashirin's incursion in Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq's reign, yet no option pairs 2 with 3, so the paper evidently treats 3 as incorrect.

items.value: The Sayyids were known as Kulah-Daran
items.reasoning: Kulah-daran is Persian for 'cap-wearers', from kulah, a cap, and the term is used in medieval Indian usage for the Sayyids, who were distinguished by their headgear. The competing reading is the Qalandars, the wandering dervishes who also wore a distinctive cap, and I cannot separate the two from the stem alone; Arab merchants and Persian calligraphists have no connection with the term. Answered as Sayyids with low confidence.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct
items.reasoning: Albuquerque took Goa in 1510 from the Adil Shahi ruler of Bijapur, so statement 2 holds, and Francis Day obtained the Madraspatnam strip in 1639 on lease from Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka, a Nayaka feudatory of the Vijayanagara ruler then at Chandragiri, so statement 3 holds. Statement 1 fails: the Dutch got Masulipatnam from Golconda in 1605 and Pulicat in 1610 from the local Vijayanagara-linked authority, while by the time they reached Odisha at Pipli and Balasore the Gajapati power had long been displaced by Afghan and then Mughal rule.

items.value: All three statements about slavery in the Arthashastra are correct
items.reasoning: Kautilya's list of types of dasa includes the dandapranita, a person reduced to slavery by way of judicial punishment, which validates statement 1. The Arthashastra further lays down that when a master begets a son on his own female slave, both the mother and the child are to be held free, which validates statement 2, and that such a son is entitled to the standing and share of the master's own son, which validates statement 3. All three come from the same section of Book III on slaves and labourers.

items.value: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct; devaluation raises rather than reduces currency risk on ECBs
items.reasoning: A tightening US Federal Reserve raises dollar returns and pulls portfolio capital out of emerging markets, which is capital flight, so statement 1 holds. That outflow depreciates the rupee and pushes up domestic and global funding costs, raising the effective servicing cost of firms already carrying External Commercial Borrowings, so statement 2 holds. Statement 3 inverts the logic: an unhedged ECB is repaid in foreign currency, so a weaker rupee means more rupees per dollar of debt and therefore greater, not lesser, currency risk.

items.value: Only three of the four, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh and Tripura, are known tea-producing States
items.reasoning: Kerala grows tea on the Munnar and Wayanad slopes, Himachal Pradesh is the home of the GI-tagged Kangra tea, and Tripura is one of the recognised tea-growing States of the North-East with a sizeable estate sector. Andhra Pradesh is not a tea State; its Araku valley is known for coffee, not tea. Hence three of the four.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct; credit rating agencies are regulated by SEBI, not the RBI
items.reasoning: Credit rating agencies in India are registered and regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) Regulations, 1999, so statement 1 is wrong; the RBI only accredits agencies for specific regulatory purposes such as bank capital norms. ICRA Limited is indeed a public limited company whose shares are listed on the stock exchanges, and Brickwork Ratings is a Bengaluru-based Indian rating agency, so statements 2 and 3 both hold.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct; the RBI Governor is not the Chairman of the Banks Board Bureau
items.reasoning: The Banks Board Bureau was headed by an independent chairman, Vinod Rai at its inception and later B. P. Sharma, with an RBI Deputy Governor among its ex-officio members; the RBI Governor was never its chairman, so statement 1 fails. Its declared mandate was to recommend candidates for the posts of whole-time directors and non-executive chairmen of public sector banks and financial institutions, and to help those banks frame business strategies and capital raising plans, which is exactly statements 2 and 3.

items.value: Both statements about convertible bonds are correct
items.reasoning: A convertible bond bundles a plain bond with an option to convert into equity, and the issuer charges for that option by paying a lower coupon than a comparable straight bond, which is statement 1. Statement 2 follows from the same option: because share prices tend over time to move with the general price level, the right to convert gives the holder partial protection against rising consumer prices that a fixed-coupon bond does not have. Statement 2 is the judgement call, since the hedge is only approximate, but it is the standard textbook claim.

items.value: India is a member of all three: AIIB, MTCR and SCO
items.reasoning: India is a founding member of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and its second largest shareholder after China; it joined the Missile Technology Control Regime in June 2016 as its thirty-fifth member; and it became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in 2017 alongside Pakistan. All three therefore apply.

items.value: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct
items.reasoning: Vietnam has been among the world's fastest growing economies in recent years, its growth resting on deep integration into global manufacturing supply chains and an export-led model, and it has long drawn global manufacturers with low labour costs and a managed, stable exchange rate, so statements 1, 3 and 4 hold. Statement 2 is plainly wrong: Vietnam is a one-party state led by the Communist Party of Vietnam. Statement 5, a claim to the most productive e-service sector in the Indo-Pacific, is an unsupported superlative.

items.value: The Reserve Bank of India is responsible for maintaining price stability by controlling inflation
items.reasoning: Under the amended RBI Act and the monetary policy framework agreement, the primary objective of monetary policy is price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth, and the Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI is charged with meeting the inflation target notified by the Government. The Department of Consumer Affairs only monitors prices of essential commodities, and the Financial Stability and Development Council is a coordination body for financial stability, not an inflation authority.

items.value: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct; NFTs are precisely not exchangeable at equivalency
items.reasoning: A non-fungible token is a unique cryptographic token recorded on a blockchain, and one of its uses is to represent an underlying physical asset in digital form, so statements 1 and 2 hold. Statement 3 contradicts the defining property: 'non-fungible' means each token is unique and cannot be swapped one-for-one at equivalency, which is what disqualifies NFTs as a medium of exchange, unlike fungible cryptocurrencies.

items.value: Three pairs are not correctly matched: Ghataprabha, Indira Sagar and Maithon
items.reasoning: Only Gandhi Sagar is correctly placed, being the Chambal reservoir in Madhya Pradesh. Ghataprabha is a Krishna tributary dammed at Hidkal in Karnataka, not Telangana; the Indira Sagar reservoir is on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh, not Andhra Pradesh; and Maithon on the Barakar is a Damodar Valley Corporation reservoir in Jharkhand, not Chhattisgarh. Three mismatches.

items.value: The Labour Bureau compiles this information
items.reasoning: The Labour Bureau, an attached office of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, is the agency that collects and publishes statistics on industrial disputes, closures, retrenchments and lay-offs, alongside its consumer price index and wage series. The Central Statistics Office handles national accounts and the industrial production index, DPIIT deals with industrial policy and FDI, and NTMIS tracks technical manpower.

items.value: Statements 1, 2 and 3 describe the Coal Controller's role; delivery to end users in time does not
items.reasoning: The Coal Controller's Organisation is the government's principal source of coal statistics, it monitors the development of captive coal and lignite blocks, and the Coal Controller acts as the competent authority under the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957 to hear objections to acquisition notifications, so statements 1, 2 and 3 hold. Statement 4 is a commercial supply obligation between miner and consumer, enforced through fuel supply agreements, not a regulatory function of the CCO.

items.value: Bringing an area under the Fifth Schedule would prevent transfer of tribal land to non-tribals
items.reasoning: The core operative power in the Fifth Schedule is the Governor's authority to make regulations for a Scheduled Area, expressly including regulations that prohibit or restrict the transfer of land by or among members of the Scheduled Tribes, which is what option A states. Scheduled Area status does not create a local self-governing body, since the Tribes Advisory Council is only advisory and Panchayati Raj there flows from PESA; nor does it convert the area into a Union Territory or confer Special Category status, which is a Planning Commission and finance construct.

items.value: Only statement 2, about the National Institute of Urban Affairs, is correct
items.reasoning: The India Sanitation Coalition is an industry-led platform convened under FICCI to promote safe and sustainable sanitation, drawing on corporate and CSR support; it is not a body funded by the Government of India and the World Health Organization, so statement 1 fails. The National Institute of Urban Affairs is the premier autonomous institute under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for urban research, capacity building and knowledge dissemination, which is what statement 2 asserts.

items.value: The Central Ground Water Authority was constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
items.reasoning: The Central Ground Water Authority was constituted by notification under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, following Supreme Court directions, to regulate and control groundwater development and management. The Central Water Commission and the Central Ground Water Board are attached and subordinate offices of the water ministry created by executive order, and the National Water Development Agency is a registered society, so none of them derives from the 1986 Act.
